transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just… I can’t shake this heavy feeling. It’s like this hopelessness has settled over everything, and I keep trying to tell myself to get up, to handle things, to be practical about it, but I can’t seem to move out from under it.

After the divorce, I really tried to rebuild my life, you know? I thought I was putting pieces back together—work, routines, just trying to make something solid again—and now it feels like all of that has collapsed. Like everything I built is just sitting on top of me, and I’m stuck underneath it. I don’t really know what else to do, so… that’s why I’m here.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hopeless feeling?

About a month, I think. It didn’t happen all at once, exactly, but it started really settling in around when the financial mess after the divorce became… unavoidable, I guess. Like the paperwork and bills and all the practical things I thought I could manage started piling up, and then this heaviness just kind of came down over everything.

At first I kept telling myself it was just stress, that anyone would feel overwhelmed, and maybe if I got organized or made a plan it would ease up. But it’s been hanging over me for weeks now—about a month—and it hasn’t really lifted.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before this heavy feeling started?

I’m… not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I know I’m not myself, but when you say “enjoying things,” it’s hard for me to separate what I actually don’t enjoy anymore from what I just haven’t really had the energy or space to even think about.

Before all this, I had things that felt normal or comforting, but lately everything is sort of filtered through this heaviness, if that makes sense. I’ll try to do something familiar and I’m half there, half thinking about everything that’s wrong, so it’s difficult to tell whether the thing itself doesn’t feel good anymore or whether I’m just… buried under everything.

So I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed clear enjoyment the way I used to, but I also don’t know if I can give you a clean yes or no. Everything just feels kind of muted right now.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

I don’t know that I can point to anything and say, yes, that still gives me real pleasure. That’s part of what feels so unsettling. I’ll do things sometimes because I know they’re things I used to like, or because they’re supposed to help, or because I’m trying not to just sit there with the heaviness, but it doesn’t really land the same way.

It’s more like… I might have a moment where something is distracting, maybe, or familiar, but I wouldn’t call it pleasure exactly. It’s like the volume has been turned way down on everything. And then I start questioning myself—am I not enjoying it, or am I just so preoccupied that I can’t access that feeling? I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed anything recently that really cuts through it.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. I… I have. It’s hard to say out loud, because I don’t think of myself as someone who would say that, but since this started I’ve had thoughts like… it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Not exactly like I’m calmly deciding something, more like I’m so tired and everything feels so impossible that not having to face another day starts to sound like relief.

And I tried to tell myself it was just a passing thought, like people say things when they’re overwhelmed, but it got stronger than that. There was a point where it scared me because it didn’t feel like just some distant, dramatic thought anymore—it felt too close, like I couldn’t trust where my mind was going. So I called the employee assistance program through work. I didn’t really know what else to do, and I was embarrassed, honestly, but I scared myself enough that I made the call.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since this heavy feeling started?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking it closely, and I don’t think I’ve noticed some obvious dramatic change where my clothes suddenly fit completely differently or anything like that.

It’s possible there’s been some change, but I can’t confidently say. I’ve been so focused on just getting through the day that I haven’t been paying much attention to the scale or even to my body in that way. I guess if you’re asking whether I’ve clearly lost or gained a lot, I don’t think I can say that I have. I just don’t know for sure.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since this heavy feeling started?

Yes, definitely. Sleep has been… really bad. It’s not just that I’m going to bed late or something normal like that. I’ll be exhausted, like my body feels heavy and I know I should be able to sleep, but then I just lie there staring at the ceiling.

My mind starts replaying everything — bills, things I’m behind on, mistakes I might have made at work, things I said wrong or forgot to do — and it just loops. I’ll think I’ve settled down, and then another thought comes in and I’m wide awake again.

And then other nights, or sometimes the same night, I’ll wake up before dawn and it feels like I never really slept at all. Like I must have been asleep at some point, but I don’t feel rested. I just wake up already tense and tired, and then I’m stuck there waiting for the day to start.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done physically since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. Very much. Everything feels slowed down, like I’m trying to move through something thick. Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. I know that sounds dramatic, but that’s honestly the closest way I can describe it.

Even things that should be automatic feel like they require this huge negotiation with myself. Taking a shower, getting dressed, opening my laptop… it’s like I look at the thing and I understand what needs to happen, but my body just doesn’t want to start. Or it starts, but every step feels heavier than it should.

At work especially, I’ll sit there knowing I need to answer an email or pull up a file, and it feels almost ridiculous how much effort it takes just to begin. It’s not that I don’t care. I do care, and that almost makes it worse, because I can see the work piling up and I’m just… not able to move through it the way I normally would.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety since this heavy feeling started?

Yes, but it’s a little confusing because at the same time I feel slowed down and heavy. It’s like physically I’m exhausted, but I also can’t just sit still with it.

I’ve been pacing around my apartment a lot, especially when there’s nothing useful left to do. I’ll walk from the kitchen to the living room and back again, checking my phone, opening my laptop, closing it, standing up again. It doesn’t even feel productive half the time, just this internal pressure like I should be doing something.

And at work, or around work, I started pushing myself into extra things — like extra proposals, calling colleagues because I suddenly had another idea, volunteering for tasks that no one actually asked me to take on. I’d tell myself, “If I just take care of this one more thing, maybe I’ll feel less awful,” but then it would turn into five things.

So yes, restless is probably the right word. Not always fidgety in a small way, but more like I can’t settle, and I keep trying to force myself into activity even when I don’t have the energy for it.
Have you been feeling guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother you since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. Constantly. And it’s not even proportional to what actually happened, I know that somewhere in my head, but it doesn’t feel that way.

I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer. Like if I miss something small, or I have to double-check a calculation, or someone sends back a comment on a plan, my brain turns it into this whole indictment of me as a person. I’ll replay it over and over, like, “How could you miss that? What if that caused a bigger problem? What if everyone knows you’re barely holding it together?” Even tense emails — not even openly hostile ones, just slightly curt or corrective — I’ll read them again and again and think, “See, you’re ruining things. You’re making everyone else’s job harder.”

And it’s not just work. I keep thinking I’m a failed wife, like I should be better, warmer, more present, less exhausting to be around. I feel like a burden. Like people have to manage me, or make allowances for me, or tiptoe around me, and then I feel guilty for that too.

It’s like every little mistake becomes proof of some bigger failure. A missed calculation, a delayed response, a tense conversation — I collect them in my head and use them against myself. I don’t want to, but I do.
Have you felt like you're moving or reacting more slowly than usual since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. I mean, it feels less like I’m choosing to move slowly and more like everything takes this unreasonable amount of effort now.

Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. I’ll know exactly what I need to do, but getting myself to actually do it physically — opening the laptop, starting a task, even just shifting from one thing to the next — feels like I’m trying to push through something heavy. It’s embarrassing because these are basic things, things I normally don’t even think about.

Even taking a shower can feel like this whole project. Not emotionally in some dramatic way, just… the energy required to stand up, get the towel, turn on the water, wash my hair — it feels like more than I have available. And then I get frustrated with myself because I’m like, “Why is this so hard? It’s just a shower.”

So yes, I do feel slower. My reactions, my movements, my ability to get started — all of it feels delayed, like my body is lagging behind what my mind is telling it to do.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense irritability since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. I mean… yes, definitely, though it’s hard to separate it from everything else because before I got to this heavy crash, I was kind of all over the place emotionally.

There were times when I felt almost strangely wired, like everything was finally clicking and I could see exactly what needed to happen, and I was talking faster and pushing things forward because it all felt so obvious to me. And then if someone in a meeting slowed it down or questioned a detail, I would get irritated really fast. Not just mildly annoyed — I’d snap. Over things that, normally, I think I would have just discussed or let go.

Like someone would make a small comment on a design approach or ask for clarification, and I’d hear it as them being obstructive or missing the point, and I’d respond sharply. Then later I’d think, “Why did I come at them like that?” because the comment itself wasn’t that big of a deal. It was like I had no buffer. Everything felt urgent, and anyone not moving at the same pace felt like they were in the way.

So yes, intense irritability happened. It wasn’t constant every second, but when it came up it was much stronger than my usual reaction, and it came out at people in meetings over really small things.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy before this heavy feeling started that you have not done at all since it began?

I’m not sure I can point to something I’ve done absolutely none of, if that makes sense. I mean, there are things I’ve done less, or things that feel harder to start, but “not at all” is harder for me to answer cleanly.

I don’t know if I’ve been keeping track very well, honestly. A lot of it just blurs together, and then I start questioning whether I really stopped doing something or whether I just did it once and it barely counted. So… I don’t want to overstate it.

There are definitely things that don’t feel the same or that I don’t reach for as naturally, but I’m not sure there’s a specific activity I used to enjoy that I can confidently say I have not done at all since this started.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy since this heavy feeling started?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that cleanly.

I don’t know if it’s exactly that I’ve lost interest, like the interest has disappeared, or if everything just feels so hard to access right now that it looks the same from the outside. Because there are things I know I normally like — or at least I remember liking them — but when I think about actually doing them, it feels like there’s this wall between me and the activity.

So I guess I’d say I haven’t felt drawn to things the way I usually do. But I’m hesitant to say, “Yes, I’ve lost interest,” as if I feel nothing about them, because sometimes I’ll think, “I should want to do that,” or “That used to help,” and there’s still some part of me that knows it matters. It’s just not pulling me in.

It’s more like the spark is muted. Or like the idea of enjoying something feels theoretical. I can recognize that something is supposed to be enjoyable, but I don’t feel naturally motivated toward it. And then I get stuck trying to figure out whether that counts as loss of interest or just being too weighed down to follow through.

So… yes, maybe somewhat, but I’m not confident labeling it. I’ve noticed things don’t feel as appealing or easy to engage with, but I can’t give you a neat answer beyond that.
Have you been feeling worthless since this heavy feeling started?

Yes. Very much, actually.

It’s not just feeling bad about myself in a general way. It’s like my brain keeps building a case against me, over and over. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly I’m telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, like I shouldn’t be trusted with anything important, and then I start replaying every missed calculation or every tense email or every time I didn’t explain something clearly enough as if it proves I ruin things.

And it doesn’t stay only at work. It spills into everything. I keep thinking I’m a failed wife, like I’m not showing up the way I’m supposed to, like being around me is just exhausting or disappointing. Then that turns into this thought that I’m a burden — at home, at work, everywhere. Like people would have an easier time if they didn’t have to deal with me.

I know, on some level, that one mistake or one awkward email shouldn’t mean all of that. If someone else said this about themselves, I’d probably tell them they were being unfair. But when it’s me, it feels convincing. I just keep going back through things, picking out evidence that I’m failing, and it’s hard to stop once it starts.
Do you feel like your heavy feeling has been getting worse over the past month?

Yes… I think it has. Or maybe it’s that I’ve become less able to push it aside.

When I came in, it was because I just couldn’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling anymore. It feels like everything I built after the divorce — all the stability, the work I put into seeming okay, making a life that was supposed to be mine again — has just collapsed. And I’m sitting under it, like I can see the shape of what it used to be, but I can’t get out from underneath it.

Over the past month, that feeling has felt more constant. It’s not just a bad evening or a rough couple of days where I can say, “Okay, you’re stressed, sleep it off.” It’s more like I wake up and it’s already there, this weight in the room with me. And I keep trying to tell myself I’ve handled hard things before, especially after the divorce, but lately that thought doesn’t comfort me. It almost makes it worse, because I look at what I rebuilt and think, how did I let it all fall apart again?

So… yes. Worse, or at least heavier. More hopeless. Harder to get away from.
Have you experienced any periods where your heavy feeling lifted or improved significantly since it started?

Not really. I mean… I’ve had moments where I’ve been distracted, maybe, or where I can go through a task and look functional from the outside, but I wouldn’t say the heavy feeling has lifted in any real way.

That’s actually part of why I came in. I kept waiting for it to pass, like maybe if I got through the week or slept on it or just stopped thinking so much, it would loosen. But it hasn’t. It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling that I can’t shake. It feels like everything I built after the divorce — all the effort to make my life stable again, to feel like I had rebuilt something — has collapsed, and I’m just sitting underneath it.

So there might be little stretches where I’m not actively focusing on it every second, but it doesn’t feel like improvement. It’s more like the weight is still there, even if I’m temporarily looking somewhere else. I haven’t had a period where I thought, “Oh, I’m coming out of this,” or where I felt significantly lighter.
Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt better and the heavy feeling was not as strong?

No… not for two weeks. I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.

There are small bits of time where I’m distracted enough that I’m not actively thinking about it — like I can focus on something in front of me for a little while — but the heavy feeling is still there underneath. It doesn’t feel like it actually lets up.

I came in because I can’t shake it. It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I worked so hard to build after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under all of it. So no, I wouldn’t say there’s been a stretch where I felt better for a couple weeks or where it was really not as strong. It’s been more constant than that.
Has your heavy feeling lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes. I mean… yes, that’s exactly how it’s been. It’s not like it comes and goes in a clean way, where I can point to a day and say, “That was a better day.” It’s been there most of the day, almost every day.

I came in because I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I worked so hard to build after the divorce — the stability, the sense that I had gotten my life back into some kind of shape — has collapsed. And I’m just… sitting under it. Even when I’m doing something else, it feels like it’s still there in the background, pressing down.

So yes, for at least two weeks. More than that, really. It’s felt constant enough that I stopped being able to tell myself it was just a bad day or a rough stretch.
Has your heavy feeling lasted for at least two months?

No… I don’t think it’s been two months. It feels longer, honestly, because every day has been so heavy, but if I’m trying to be accurate, it’s been about a month.

It really started hanging over me around the time the financial mess from the divorce came up again. That’s when it felt like the floor just dropped out. Since then it’s been pretty constant, but not two full months yet. More like… roughly a month of feeling like this.

patient.answer:
About a month, I think. It didn’t happen all at once, exactly, but it started really settling in around when the financial mess after the divorce became… unavoidable, I guess. Like the paperwork and bills and all the practical things I thought I could manage started piling up, and then this heaviness just kind of came down over everything.

At first I kept telling myself it was just stress, that anyone would feel overwhelmed, and maybe if I got organized or made a plan it would ease up. But it’s been hanging over me for weeks now—about a month—and it hasn’t really lifted.

patient.answer:
Yes, definitely. Sleep has been… really bad. It’s not just that I’m going to bed late or something normal like that. I’ll be exhausted, like my body feels heavy and I know I should be able to sleep, but then I just lie there staring at the ceiling.

My mind starts replaying everything — bills, things I’m behind on, mistakes I might have made at work, things I said wrong or forgot to do — and it just loops. I’ll think I’ve settled down, and then another thought comes in and I’m wide awake again.

And then other nights, or sometimes the same night, I’ll wake up before dawn and it feels like I never really slept at all. Like I must have been asleep at some point, but I don’t feel rested. I just wake up already tense and tired, and then I’m stuck there waiting for the day to start.

doctor.intent: determine presence of psychomotor agitation or retardation
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done physically since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete, and even taking a shower or opening my laptop takes more energy than I seem to have.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about physical slowing and difficulty getting things done, which is most directly covered by the fatigue/lack of energy symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yes. Very much. Everything feels slowed down, like I’m trying to move through something thick. Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. I know that sounds dramatic, but that’s honestly the closest way I can describe it.

Even things that should be automatic feel like they require this huge negotiation with myself. Taking a shower, getting dressed, opening my laptop… it’s like I look at the thing and I understand what needs to happen, but my body just doesn’t want to start. Or it starts, but every step feels heavier than it should.

At work especially, I’ll sit there knowing I need to answer an email or pull up a file, and it feels almost ridiculous how much effort it takes just to begin. It’s not that I don’t care. I do care, and that almost makes it worse, because I can see the work piling up and I’m just… not able to move through it the way I normally would.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor agitation
doctor.question: Have you been feeling restless or fidgety since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
target_item.manifestation: I started pushing myself into extra proposals, calling colleagues with new ideas, volunteering for tasks no one asked me to take on, and pacing around my apartment when there was nothing useful left to do.

patient.answer:
Yes, but it’s a little confusing because at the same time I feel slowed down and heavy. It’s like physically I’m exhausted, but I also can’t just sit still with it.

I’ve been pacing around my apartment a lot, especially when there’s nothing useful left to do. I’ll walk from the kitchen to the living room and back again, checking my phone, opening my laptop, closing it, standing up again. It doesn’t even feel productive half the time, just this internal pressure like I should be doing something.

And at work, or around work, I started pushing myself into extra things — like extra proposals, calling colleagues because I suddenly had another idea, volunteering for tasks that no one actually asked me to take on. I’d tell myself, “If I just take care of this one more thing, maybe I’ll feel less awful,” but then it would turn into five things.

So yes, restless is probably the right word. Not always fidgety in a small way, but more like I can’t settle, and I keep trying to force myself into activity even when I don’t have the energy for it.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of guilt
doctor.question: Have you been feeling guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother you since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, a failed wife, and a burden, and I replay every missed calculation or tense email like proof that I ruin things.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly asking about excessive or unusual guilt since the depressive symptoms began.

patient.answer:
Yes. Constantly. And it’s not even proportional to what actually happened, I know that somewhere in my head, but it doesn’t feel that way.

I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer. Like if I miss something small, or I have to double-check a calculation, or someone sends back a comment on a plan, my brain turns it into this whole indictment of me as a person. I’ll replay it over and over, like, “How could you miss that? What if that caused a bigger problem? What if everyone knows you’re barely holding it together?” Even tense emails — not even openly hostile ones, just slightly curt or corrective — I’ll read them again and again and think, “See, you’re ruining things. You’re making everyone else’s job harder.”

And it’s not just work. I keep thinking I’m a failed wife, like I should be better, warmer, more present, less exhausting to be around. I feel like a burden. Like people have to manage me, or make allowances for me, or tiptoe around me, and then I feel guilty for that too.

It’s like every little mistake becomes proof of some bigger failure. A missed calculation, a delayed response, a tense conversation — I collect them in my head and use them against myself. I don’t want to, but I do.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of psychomotor agitation or retardation to differentiate between F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, and F32.3
doctor.question: Have you felt like you're moving or reacting more slowly than usual since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete, and even taking a shower or opening my laptop takes more energy than I seem to have.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about feeling slowed down and having difficulty physically getting through activities, which is best captured by the fatigue/lack of energy profile.

patient.answer:
Yes. I mean, it feels less like I’m choosing to move slowly and more like everything takes this unreasonable amount of effort now.

Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. I’ll know exactly what I need to do, but getting myself to actually do it physically — opening the laptop, starting a task, even just shifting from one thing to the next — feels like I’m trying to push through something heavy. It’s embarrassing because these are basic things, things I normally don’t even think about.

Even taking a shower can feel like this whole project. Not emotionally in some dramatic way, just… the energy required to stand up, get the towel, turn on the water, wash my hair — it feels like more than I have available. And then I get frustrated with myself because I’m like, “Why is this so hard? It’s just a shower.”

So yes, I do feel slower. My reactions, my movements, my ability to get started — all of it feels delayed, like my body is lagging behind what my mind is telling it to do.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Have you experienced any episodes of intense irritability since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Before this crash, I was either weirdly wired and convinced everything was finally clicking, or I was snapping at people in meetings over tiny comments that normally wouldn’t bother me.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly asking about episodes of intense irritability, which matches the irritable mood component of this symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yes. I mean… yes, definitely, though it’s hard to separate it from everything else because before I got to this heavy crash, I was kind of all over the place emotionally.

There were times when I felt almost strangely wired, like everything was finally clicking and I could see exactly what needed to happen, and I was talking faster and pushing things forward because it all felt so obvious to me. And then if someone in a meeting slowed it down or questioned a detail, I would get irritated really fast. Not just mildly annoyed — I’d snap. Over things that, normally, I think I would have just discussed or let go.

Like someone would make a small comment on a design approach or ask for clarification, and I’d hear it as them being obstructive or missing the point, and I’d respond sharply. Then later I’d think, “Why did I come at them like that?” because the comment itself wasn’t that big of a deal. It was like I had no buffer. Everything felt urgent, and anyone not moving at the same pace felt like they were in the way.

So yes, intense irritability happened. It wasn’t constant every second, but when it came up it was much stronger than my usual reaction, and it came out at people in meetings over really small things.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of loss of interest in activities
doctor.question: Are there any activities that you used to enjoy before this heavy feeling started that you have not done at all since it began?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, but the provided symptom profile does not include an anhedonia item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can point to something I’ve done absolutely none of, if that makes sense. I mean, there are things I’ve done less, or things that feel harder to start, but “not at all” is harder for me to answer cleanly.

I don’t know if I’ve been keeping track very well, honestly. A lot of it just blurs together, and then I start questioning whether I really stopped doing something or whether I just did it once and it barely counted. So… I don’t want to overstate it.

There are definitely things that don’t feel the same or that I don’t reach for as naturally, but I’m not sure there’s a specific activity I used to enjoy that I can confidently say I have not done at all since this started.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of loss of interest in activities
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.reason: The question is directly about loss of interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, but the provided symptom profile does not include an anhedonia/loss-of-interest item.

patient.answer:
I’m… not totally sure how to answer that cleanly.

I don’t know if it’s exactly that I’ve lost interest, like the interest has disappeared, or if everything just feels so hard to access right now that it looks the same from the outside. Because there are things I know I normally like — or at least I remember liking them — but when I think about actually doing them, it feels like there’s this wall between me and the activity.

So I guess I’d say I haven’t felt drawn to things the way I usually do. But I’m hesitant to say, “Yes, I’ve lost interest,” as if I feel nothing about them, because sometimes I’ll think, “I should want to do that,” or “That used to help,” and there’s still some part of me that knows it matters. It’s just not pulling me in.

It’s more like the spark is muted. Or like the idea of enjoying something feels theoretical. I can recognize that something is supposed to be enjoyable, but I don’t feel naturally motivated toward it. And then I get stuck trying to figure out whether that counts as loss of interest or just being too weighed down to follow through.

So… yes, maybe somewhat, but I’m not confident labeling it. I’ve noticed things don’t feel as appealing or easy to engage with, but I can’t give you a neat answer beyond that.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of worthlessness
doctor.question: Have you been feeling worthless since this heavy feeling started?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, a failed wife, and a burden, and I replay every missed calculation or tense email like proof that I ruin things.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether I have been feeling worthless since the heavy depressive feeling started.

patient.answer:
Yes. Very much, actually.

It’s not just feeling bad about myself in a general way. It’s like my brain keeps building a case against me, over and over. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly I’m telling myself I’m a terrible engineer, like I shouldn’t be trusted with anything important, and then I start replaying every missed calculation or every tense email or every time I didn’t explain something clearly enough as if it proves I ruin things.

And it doesn’t stay only at work. It spills into everything. I keep thinking I’m a failed wife, like I’m not showing up the way I’m supposed to, like being around me is just exhausting or disappointing. Then that turns into this thought that I’m a burden — at home, at work, everywhere. Like people would have an easier time if they didn’t have to deal with me.

I know, on some level, that one mistake or one awkward email shouldn’t mean all of that. If someone else said this about themselves, I’d probably tell them they were being unfair. But when it’s me, it feels convincing. I just keep going back through things, picking out evidence that I’m failing, and it’s hard to stop once it starts.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel like your heavy feeling has been getting worse over the past month?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about the course of the patient’s heavy, hopeless mood over the past month, which corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it has. Or maybe it’s that I’ve become less able to push it aside.

When I came in, it was because I just couldn’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling anymore. It feels like everything I built after the divorce — all the stability, the work I put into seeming okay, making a life that was supposed to be mine again — has just collapsed. And I’m sitting under it, like I can see the shape of what it used to be, but I can’t get out from underneath it.

Over the past month, that feeling has felt more constant. It’s not just a bad evening or a rough couple of days where I can say, “Okay, you’re stressed, sleep it off.” It’s more like I wake up and it’s already there, this weight in the room with me. And I keep trying to tell myself I’ve handled hard things before, especially after the divorce, but lately that thought doesn’t comfort me. It almost makes it worse, because I look at what I rebuilt and think, how did I let it all fall apart again?

So… yes. Worse, or at least heavier. More hopeless. Harder to get away from.

inference.note: F32.0 and F32.1 were ruled out due to the presence of significant guilt, worthlessness, and suicidal ideation, which are more characteristic of F32.2 and F32.3

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms to differentiate between F32.2 and F32.3
doctor.question: Have you experienced any periods where your heavy feeling lifted or improved significantly since it started?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the course of the heavy, hopeless mood—whether the depressed mood has lifted or improved since it began.

patient.answer:
Not really. I mean… I’ve had moments where I’ve been distracted, maybe, or where I can go through a task and look functional from the outside, but I wouldn’t say the heavy feeling has lifted in any real way.

That’s actually part of why I came in. I kept waiting for it to pass, like maybe if I got through the week or slept on it or just stopped thinking so much, it would loosen. But it hasn’t. It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling that I can’t shake. It feels like everything I built after the divorce — all the effort to make my life stable again, to feel like I had rebuilt something — has collapsed, and I’m just sitting underneath it.

So there might be little stretches where I’m not actively focusing on it every second, but it doesn’t feel like improvement. It’s more like the weight is still there, even if I’m temporarily looking somewhere else. I haven’t had a period where I thought, “Oh, I’m coming out of this,” or where I felt significantly lighter.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt better and the heavy feeling was not as strong?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether the depressed/heavy hopeless mood has persisted or significantly improved for at least two weeks.

patient.answer:
No… not for two weeks. I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.

There are small bits of time where I’m distracted enough that I’m not actively thinking about it — like I can focus on something in front of me for a little while — but the heavy feeling is still there underneath. It doesn’t feel like it actually lets up.

I came in because I can’t shake it. It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I worked so hard to build after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under all of it. So no, I wouldn’t say there’s been a stretch where I felt better for a couple weeks or where it was really not as strong. It’s been more constant than that.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of the patient's current depressive episode to differentiate between F32.2 and F32.3
doctor.question: Has your heavy feeling lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed and I’m just sitting under it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the heavy, hopeless feeling has been present most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks, which directly assesses persistent depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yes. I mean… yes, that’s exactly how it’s been. It’s not like it comes and goes in a clean way, where I can point to a day and say, “That was a better day.” It’s been there most of the day, almost every day.

I came in because I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I worked so hard to build after the divorce — the stability, the sense that I had gotten my life back into some kind of shape — has collapsed. And I’m just… sitting under it. Even when I’m doing something else, it feels like it’s still there in the background, pressing down.

So yes, for at least two weeks. More than that, really. It’s felt constant enough that I stopped being able to tell myself it was just a bad day or a rough stretch.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for a depressive episode
doctor.question: Has your heavy feeling lasted for at least two months?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression has been hanging over me for about a month, starting around the financial mess after the divorce.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the depressive heavy feeling has lasted, which is directly covered by the depressive episode duration profile.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think it’s been two months. It feels longer, honestly, because every day has been so heavy, but if I’m trying to be accurate, it’s been about a month.

It really started hanging over me around the time the financial mess from the divorce came up again. That’s when it felt like the floor just dropped out. Since then it’s been pretty constant, but not two full months yet. More like… roughly a month of feeling like this.
